passages.text: Later on, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife. “I want to go to my wife in her room,” he said. But her father would not let him enter.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
He was strong.
He had a Philistine wife.
Some time passed.
It was the time of the wheat harvest.
Samson took a young goat.
He went to visit his wife.
Samson said, “I want to go to my wife in her room.”
Her father did not let him enter.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י מִיָּמִ֜ים בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר־ חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּפְקֹ֨ד שִׁמְשׁ֤וֹן אֶת־ אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ בִּגְדִ֣י עִזִּ֔ים וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָבֹ֥אָה אֶל־ אִשְׁתִּ֖י הֶחָ֑דְרָה וְלֹֽא־ נְתָנ֥וֹ אָבִ֖יהָ לָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: “I was sure that you thoroughly hated her,” said her father, “so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.”
passages.sermon:
Samson’s father-in-law spoke to Samson.
He said, “I thought you hated my daughter.”
“I gave her to your companion.”
“Her younger sister is more beautiful than she is.”
“Please take her instead.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֗יהָ אָמֹ֤ר אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ כִּי־ שָׂנֹ֣א שְׂנֵאתָ֔הּ וָאֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה לְמֵרֵעֶ֑ךָ הֲלֹ֨א אֲחֹתָ֤הּ הַקְּטַנָּה֙ טוֹבָ֣ה מִמֶּ֔נָּה תְּהִי־ נָ֥א לְךָ֖ תַּחְתֶּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Samson said to them, “This time I will be blameless in doing harm to the Philistines.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson spoke to the people.
Samson said, “This time I am not guilty before the Philistines.
I will do them harm.
I will not be blamed for what I do to them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן נִקֵּ֥יתִי הַפַּ֖עַם מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים כִּֽי־ עֹשֶׂ֥ה אֲנִ֛י עִמָּ֖ם רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. And he took torches, turned the foxes tail-to-tail, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson was very strong.
Samson went out.
He caught three hundred foxes.
He took some torches.
He tied the foxes together in pairs by their tails.
He put one torch between the two tails of each pair.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן וַיִּלְכֹּ֖ד שְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת שׁוּעָלִ֑ים וַיִּקַּ֣ח לַפִּדִ֗ים וַיֶּ֤פֶן זָנָב֙ אֶל־ זָנָ֔ב וַיָּ֨שֶׂם לַפִּ֥יד אֶחָ֛ד בֵּין־ שְׁנֵ֥י הַזְּנָב֖וֹת בַּתָּֽוֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then he lit the torches and released the foxes into the standing grain of the Philistines, burning up the piles of grain and the standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson took torches and set them on fire.
He tied the burning torches to the foxes’ tails.
Samson released the foxes into the fields of the Philistines.
The foxes ran through the standing grain of the Philistines.
The fire burned the piles of harvested grain.
The fire also burned the standing grain in the fields.
The fire spread to the vineyards.
The fire also burned the olive groves.
passages.original: וַיַּבְעֶר־ אֵשׁ֙ בַּלַּפִּידִ֔ים וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח בְּקָמ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּבְעֵ֛ר מִגָּדִ֥ישׁ וְעַד־ קָמָ֖ה וְעַד־ כֶּ֥רֶם זָֽיִת׃

passages.text: “Who did this?” the Philistines demanded. “It was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite,” they were told. “For his wife was given to his companion.” So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were a powerful enemy of Israel.
They saw that their grain, vineyards, and olive groves were burned.
The Philistines asked, “Who did this?”
People answered, “Samson did it.”
Samson was the son-in-law of the Timnite.
The Timnite’s daughter was Samson’s wife.
Her father gave her to Samson’s companion.
The Philistines heard this.
The Philistines went up to the Timnite’s house.
They burned Samson’s wife and her father with fire.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֮ מִ֣י עָ֣שָׂה זֹאת֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ חֲתַ֣ן הַתִּמְנִ֔י כִּ֚י לָקַ֣ח אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֖הּ לְמֵרֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיַּעֲל֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אוֹתָ֛הּ וְאֶת־ אָבִ֖יהָ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: And Samson told them, “Because you have done this, I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson spoke to the Philistines.
Samson said, "You have done this evil thing."
Samson said, "I will take vengeance on you."
Samson said, "I will not stop until I have punished you."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אִֽם־ תַּעֲשׂ֖וּן כָּזֹ֑את כִּ֛י אִם־ נִקַּ֥מְתִּי בָכֶ֖ם וְאַחַ֥ר אֶחְדָּֽל׃

passages.text: And he struck them ruthlessly with a great slaughter, and then went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson was very strong.
Samson attacked the Philistines.
Samson struck the Philistines with a great blow.
Samson defeated many Philistines.
Samson then went down to the rock of Etam.
Samson stayed in a cave at the rock of Etam.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨ךְ אוֹתָ֥ם שׁ֛וֹק עַל־ יָרֵ֖ךְ מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיֵּ֣רֶד וַיֵּ֔שֶׁב בִּסְעִ֖יף סֶ֥לַע עֵיטָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then the Philistines went up, camped in Judah, and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were enemies of Israel.
The Philistines went up from their land.
They entered the territory of Judah.
They set up camp in Judah.
They positioned themselves near the town of Lehi.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲל֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בִּיהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנָּטְשׁ֖וּ בַּלֶּֽחִי׃

passages.text: “Why have you attacked us?” said the men of Judah. The Philistines replied, “We have come to arrest Samson and pay him back for what he has done to us.”
passages.sermon:
The men of Judah spoke to the Philistines.
They said, “Why have you come up against us?”
The Philistines answered them.
They said, “We have come to capture Samson.”
“We want to do to him what he did to us.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה לָמָ֖ה עֲלִיתֶ֣ם עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לֶאֱס֤וֹר אֶת־ שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ עָלִ֔ינוּ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת ל֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר עָ֥שָׂה לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: In response, three thousand men of Judah went to the cave at the rock of Etam, and they asked Samson, “Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?” “I have done to them what they did to me,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Three thousand men came from the tribe of Judah.
They went down to the cave at the rock of Etam.
They spoke to Samson.
They said, “The Philistines rule over us.
Do you not know this?
What have you done to us?”
Samson answered them.
He said, “I did to them what they did to me.”
passages.original: וַיֵּרְד֡וּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אִ֜ישׁ מִֽיהוּדָ֗ה אֶל־ סְעִיף֮ סֶ֣לַע עֵיטָם֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן הֲלֹ֤א יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ כִּֽי־ מֹשְׁלִ֥ים בָּ֙נוּ֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמַה־ זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֑נוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ עָ֣שׂוּ לִ֔י כֵּ֖ן עָשִׂ֥יתִי לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: But they said to him, “We have come down to arrest you and hand you over to the Philistines.” Samson replied, “Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.”
passages.sermon:
The men of Judah spoke to Samson.
They said, “We have come down to arrest you.”
They said, “We will hand you over to the Philistines.”
Samson replied to them.
Samson said, “Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֶאֱסָרְךָ֣ יָרַ֔דְנוּ לְתִתְּךָ֖ בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הִשָּׁבְע֣וּ לִ֔י פֶּֽן־ תִּפְגְּע֥וּן בִּ֖י אַתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: “No,” they answered, “we will not kill you, but we will tie you up securely and hand you over to them.” So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.
passages.sermon:
The men of Judah spoke to Samson.
They said, “No, we will not kill you.
We will tie you up securely.
We will hand you over to the Philistines.”
They tied Samson with two new ropes.
They led Samson up from the rock.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹ֚א כִּֽי־ אָסֹ֤ר נֶֽאֱסָרְךָ֙ וּנְתַנּ֣וּךָ בְיָדָ֔ם וְהָמֵ֖ת לֹ֣א נְמִיתֶ֑ךָ וַיַּאַסְרֻ֗הוּ בִּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ עֲבֹתִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּהוּ מִן־ הַסָּֽלַע׃

passages.text: When Samson arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting against him. And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him. The ropes on his arms became like burnt flax, and the bonds broke loose from his hands.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
He was very strong.
He arrived at Lehi.
The Philistines were his enemies.
The Philistines came out to meet Samson.
They shouted against him.
The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon Samson.
The ropes were tied on Samson’s arms.
The ropes became like burnt flax.
The ropes fell off his arms.
The bonds broke loose from his hands.
passages.original: הוּא־ בָ֣א עַד־ לֶ֔חִי וּפִלְשִׁתִּ֖ים הֵרִ֣יעוּ לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַתִּצְלַ֨ח עָלָ֜יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֗ה וַתִּהְיֶ֨ינָה הָעֲבֹתִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ זְרוֹעוֹתָ֗יו כַּפִּשְׁתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּעֲר֣וּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּמַּ֥סּוּ אֱסוּרָ֖יו מֵעַ֥ל יָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson had great strength from God.
Samson found a fresh jawbone of a donkey.
He reached out his hand.
He took the jawbone.
He struck down a thousand men with it.
passages.original: וַיִּמְצָ֥א לְחִֽי־ חֲמ֖וֹר טְרִיָּ֑ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיִּקָּחֶ֔הָ וַיַּךְ־ בָּ֖הּ אֶ֥לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Then Samson said: “With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson was very strong.
God gave Samson his strength.
Samson spoke after his victory.
Samson said, “With the jawbone of a donkey, I have made heaps of men.”
Samson said, “With the jawbone of a donkey, I have killed a thousand men.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן בִּלְחִ֣י הַחֲמ֔וֹר חֲמ֖וֹר חֲמֹרָתָ֑יִם בִּלְחִ֣י הַחֲמ֔וֹר הִכֵּ֖יתִי אֶ֥לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: And when Samson had finished speaking, he cast the jawbone from his hand; and he named that place Ramath-lehi.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
He had just spoken.
He finished speaking.
He held a jawbone in his hand.
He threw the jawbone from his hand.
He named that place Ramath-lehi.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּכַלֹּת֣וֹ לְדַבֵּ֔ר וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ךְ הַלְּחִ֖י מִיָּד֑וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֛א לַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא רָ֥מַת לֶֽחִי׃

passages.text: And being very thirsty, Samson cried out to the LORD, “You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
Samson had just defeated many enemies.
Samson became very thirsty.
Samson cried out to the LORD.
Samson said, "You have given this great deliverance by your servant."
Samson said, "Now I am dying of thirst."
Samson said, "Will I fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?"
passages.original: וַיִּצְמָא֮ מְאֹד֒ וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶל־ יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אַתָּה֙ נָתַ֣תָּ בְיַֽד־ עַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶת־ הַתְּשׁוּעָ֥ה הַגְּדֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את וְעַתָּה֙ אָמ֣וּת בַּצָּמָ֔א וְנָפַלְתִּ֖י בְּיַ֥ד הָעֲרֵלִֽים׃

passages.text: So God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength returned, and he was revived. That is why he named it En-hakkore, and it remains in Lehi to this day.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God opened a hollow place in Lehi.
Water came out from the hollow place.
Samson drank the water.
Samson’s strength returned.
Samson became alive again.
Samson named the place En-hakkore.
En-hakkore is still in Lehi today.
passages.original: וַיִּבְקַ֨ע אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־ הַמַּכְתֵּ֣שׁ אֲשֶׁר־ בַּלֶּ֗חִי וַיֵּצְא֨וּ מִמֶּ֤נּוּ מַ֙יִם֙ וַיֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וַתָּ֥שָׁב רוּח֖וֹ וַיֶּ֑חִי עַל־ כֵּ֣ן׀ קָרָ֣א שְׁמָ֗הּ עֵ֤ין הַקּוֹרֵא֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלֶּ֔חִי עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
passages.sermon: Samson was a judge of Israel.\r\nHe led Israel during the time of the Philistines.\r\nHe judged Israel for twenty years.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֧ט אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בִּימֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃פ
